approach: Add `check_subjective_method(reading, request)` to crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs and one `step!(check_subjective_method(reading, request));` line at the end of `refusing_check` (checks.rs, after `check_reading_references`, so no pinned neighbour moves). Revised after round 1. The check scans only `plain_request_prose(request)` (terms.rs:189), which already drops generated root-cause lines, quoted spans, example lists, paths and fenced code. It does not scan the reading summary and has no root-cause skip. A line triggers when it holds a subjective phrase (whole words: newcomer, newcomers, how clear, clear to, clear for, clarity, easy to follow, easy to understand, easy to read, understandable) and an audience noun from the existing `VISIBLE_NOUNS` (outcome.rs:49, reused and not edited; `site` directly after `call` is ignored). Bare `readable` is not a phrase, so `human-readable` and `machine-readable` never trigger. The reading is accepted only if ONE criterion of kind Behavior (as in `check_outcome_state`, outcome.rs:323-327) holds four parts: (1) an independence word (independent, independently, fresh, separate, "no part in", "took no part", "did not build") with a reader word (reader, model, reviewer, judge); (2) a named persona (persona, newcomer, novice, beginner, first-time, or "reads it as a/an" / "reads as a/an"), not a bare "as a"; (3) a 1-to-5 scale (1 to 5, 1-5, 1–5, 1 through 5, out of 5, 5-point, five-point, or a `d/5` token); (4) a pass threshold: a threshold word (minimum, at least, below, under, threshold, "no less than") followed within three words by a digit 1-5, or a digit followed within two words by "or above/higher/more", "and above". Bare "blocks" and a digit anywhere no longer count. The error names the parts the closest Behavior criterion lacks (all four if there is none) and says to state the method as a Behavior criterion before the build. Root cause in the doc comment: no required verification method for subjective quality at the reading gate (jobs 20261014-163844-c2kt and 20261015-064153-wekz). Tests: unit tests in reading.rs, refusal-corpus cases with five new input-form tags, a declared-share test, a reading-rules line in briefs.rs, a CHANGELOG entry and a C8 row in defaults-loop.md.

decisions.choice: Put the check at the reading gate as one new `step!` line at the end of `refusing_check`; no prompt, defaults.toml or job-specific code.
decisions.reason: The fault starts where a reading with a subjective outcome and no method is accepted. `check_reading_acceptance` (checks.rs:487) is one wrapper over `refusing_check`, reached by the build path, `check_reading_text` (replay.rs:54) and `athena check-reading`, so one step covers all. The corpus test `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` forces a refusing case. Appending after `check_reading_references` keeps the adjacency tests passing.

decisions.choice: Scan only `plain_request_prose(request)`. No summary scan and no whole-request ROOT_CAUSE_ANCHOR skip (answers finding 1).
decisions.reason: `plain_request_prose` already drops the 'Fix the root cause of a repeated failure:', 'Failure class:', 'Cause:' and 'Introspection ... prevention it proposed:' lines when the anchor is present (terms.rs:62-80, 189-207; hestia.rs:480-503 builds exactly those lines). This job's request, whose cause text quotes 'a page is clear to a newcomer', therefore has no trigger left, with no special case. A root-cause job whose own sentence or acceptance bullet asks for a subjective page is still gated. The summary is model-written and is not the request's statement of the outcome, so it is not scanned.

rejected.option: Skip any request holding ROOT_CAUSE_ANCHOR and also scan the summary
rejected.why: A special case the prose filter already covers; it would let a root-cause job that delivers a subjective page through.
It would trigger on this job's own accepted reading ('such as a page being clear to a newcomer') and adds a second source of wording the request does not contain.

decisions.choice: The method must be one criterion of kind Behavior holding all four tightened parts (answers finding 2).
decisions.reason: `check_outcome_state` accepts only Behavior (outcome.rs:304-307, 323-327): a content criterion checks a file, not a run. Tight persona and threshold matchers stop incidental wording ('as a reference', a stray digit) from satisfying the gate. A unit test and a corpus case show the full method in a content criterion alone is refused. Behavior criteria are also screened by `check_criteria_evidence`, so the method must be a command the verifier can run (for example `athena audience`).

rejected.option: Accept any criterion kind with loose phrase matches
rejected.why: A content criterion or loose wording satisfies the gate with no check that runs, so the class can recur.

rejected.option: Accept parts spread over several criteria
rejected.why: No single criterion tells the verifier how to rate, and the error could not name what is missing.

rejected.option: Require the threshold to be at least 4
rejected.why: The user did not ask the gate to fix a number; left as an open question.

decisions.choice: Reuse `VISIBLE_NOUNS` as the artifact list without editing it (answers finding 4); ignore `site` right after `call`.
decisions.reason: One list means the two checks cannot drift. Editing it would also widen `delivery_verbs` (outcome.rs:200-205) and refuse more delivery requests, a different rule. Nouns such as readme or manual are left out on purpose.

rejected.option: Add readme or tutorial variants to VISIBLE_NOUNS
rejected.why: Changes check_outcome_state behaviour and its tests; out of scope for this cause.

risks.mitigation: The error lists the accepted forms and names the missing part. Unit tests cover the accepted forms (1 to 5, 1-5, out of 5, `4/5`; 'below 4', 'at least 4', '4 or above'). Widening a list later is a one-line change.
